date.label: Undated narrative of the allotment of the land
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Joshua 13–17 contains east bank and Judah/Joseph allotments, not Benjamin’s allotment (Joshua 13–17)
Caleb receives Hebron in allotment narrative (Joshua 14:6–15)
Judah city lists coexist with Jerusalem Jebusite notice (Joshua 15:1–63)
Ephraim did not expel Canaanites living in Gezer (Joshua 16:10)

connections.note: Numbers 27:1–11 records the daughters of Zelophehad's earlier legal petition, which underlies their inheritance in Joshua 17.
Numbers 36:1–12 sets out the marriage and tribal-inheritance legislation that further frames the Joshua 17 inheritance.
Numbers 32:1–42 records the Reuben and Gad east-bank negotiations and responsibilities that precede the allotments in Joshua 13.
Deuteronomy 3:12–17 concerns Moses' east-bank allocation, which Joshua 13 recapitulates rather than presenting as a separate Joshua allotment.
Judges 1:21–36 records unconquered Canaanite settlements, which complicates a simple map of comprehensive conquest.
